subject: Training deepfake detectors
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Was super impressed by your work on the Digital Media Forensics team & was curious to understand how you are thinking about responding quickly to new threats & re-training your AI / ML models. 

Many of the advanced Deepfake verification teams we work with (Onfido, iProov, Veriff, Yoti etc) complained that slow and inaccurate verification pipelines were the major bottleneck when re-training models to counter emerging threats.

At Encord we've built a multimodal data development platform - enabling verification teams to review images, videos, documents & audio in a single view - helping you to curate & annotate high quality training data at scale. 

Would love to chat / share what we've been seeing work well for Onfido, iProov, Veriff and similar partners in the space.

Would it be worth us connecting?

text:

analytics, thought you're the top leader in Iteris's detection algorithm.

subject: Tonmoy Saikia Intro | Stuttgart Coffee next week
text:
Hey [NAME],

My colleague [SENDER] recently chatted to Tonmoy who suggested that we reach out
- & as we're going to be in Stuttgart next week, thought it could be a good
opportunity to connect.

We've been working with Woven, Wayve, and Oxa's Vision teams - who faced
challenges with existing data curation & visualisation solutions (Voxel51 &
internal tools) lacking the speed & scalability required to efficiently
search through their training datasets.

searching through their datasets (using embeddings visualisations, quality
metric filters & natural language searches), enabling Vision teams to avoid
bottlenecks in model development.

from working with Woven, Wayve, Oxa, and similar partners in the space.

Will be in Stuttgart Tuesday 11th - Thursday 13th - would you be open to
meeting for a quick coffee chat?

subject: Growing the Danish Robotics team
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Was very excited to see that [COMPANY] has been growing the Robotics team & was curious to understand how you are thinking about scaling your supporting AI/CV data infrastructure as the team scales? 

Many of the CV-led Robotics teams we work with (Locus Robotics, Pickle Robot, RightHand Robotics) came to us frustrated by data preparation causing significant bottlenecks in model development. Initially they used open-source CVAT + Voxel 51 but soon found the administrative burden unmanageable as they scaled. 

At Encord we've built a scalable data management solution that brings together data curation & annotation in a single platform, freeing teams from the burden of slow, fragmented tools.

Would love to chat / share what we've been seeing work well for Locus, Pickle, & RightHand and similar Robotics partners in the space.

Would it be worth us connecting?
